=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py
  Line or code reference: Lines 264-266 (discover_manifest_via_codex) and lines 436, 502, 517, 548, 556 (open_or_update_discovery_pr)
  Problem: The discovery module catches `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, `FileNotFoundError`, and `subprocess.CalledProcessError` in its typed exception handlers, but `scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py` passes its own `CommandExecutor` (line 474: `executor=self.executor`) which wraps `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` into `CommandFailure` (line 131), wraps `FileNotFoundError` into `CommandFailure` (line 138), and raises `CommandFailure` instead of `CalledProcessError` on non-zero exits (line 147). `CommandFailure` extends `Exception` directly — not `CalledProcessError` — so every typed handler in the discovery module is bypassed in production.
  Why it fails at runtime:
  - `discover_manifest_via_codex`: codex timeout raises `CommandFailure` → not caught by `except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:` (line 264) → propagates uncaught. Same for missing codex CLI: `FileNotFoundError` → `CommandFailure` → not caught by `except FileNotFoundError:` (line 266) → propagates. The non-zero returncode path (`check=False`) is correctly handled — the `else` branch at line 278 checks `proc.returncode != 0` — so only timeout and missing-CLI are affected here.
  - `open_or_update_discovery_pr`: all git/gh commands run with `check=True`. Any failure raises `CommandFailure` → not caught by `except subprocess.CalledProcessError:` at lines 436 (gh pr list), 502 (git stage), 517 (git push — push_denied classification lost), 548 (gh pr create — label-missing fallback never triggers), 556 (retry without label). Every failure surfaces at the outer `except Exception` in `process_repository` (line 253) as `dispatch_uncaught` with no granular classification.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py
  Line or code reference: _dispatch_discovery method, lines 504-542 (disagreement branch)
  Problem: `agents.md` line 210 registers `VALIDATION_DISCOVERY_DISAGREE` as a stable log prefix (per the contractual prefix registry), but `_dispatch_discovery` never emits it. When a `type` mismatch is detected (line 502: `disagreement.disagrees is True`), the code only prints `VALIDATION_DISCOVERY_AGREE` on the match path (line 507) and `VALIDATION_DISCOVERY_PR_OPENED` or `VALIDATION_DISCOVERY_PR_REUSED` on the PR path (lines 582, 576) — never `VALIDATION_DISCOVERY_DISAGREE`.
  Why it fails at runtime: Workflow-log-analysis and drift-audit tooling that grep for the registered prefix will never observe type-mismatch events. The `VALIDATION_DISCOVERY_AGREE` prefix is emitted when types match; the corresponding disagreement counterpart is missing.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py
  Line or code reference: Line 551 (`error_text = "\n".join(part for part in (exc.stderr, exc.output) if part)`)
  Problem: The `gh pr create` error handler accesses `exc.output` (a `CalledProcessError` attribute), but when the exception mismatch is fixed and `CommandFailure` flows through this handler, `CommandFailure` provides `exc.stdout` instead of `exc.output`. The attribute `exc.output` would raise `AttributeError` on a `CommandFailure` instance.
  Why it fails at runtime: If the exception mismatch is resolved (e.g., handlers broadened to catch `CommandFailure`), the label-missing fallback path still cannot construct `error_text` because `CommandFailure` uses `stdout` not `output`. The handler would raise `AttributeError` in the except block, crashing the PR creation path.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- Requirement: "Schema: `ai-memory/schemas/validation_discovery.v1.json`" (PR Description — New / extended interfaces section). The schema file must be fetched by the orchestrator and validation workflow bootstrap steps so consumer repos can validate discovery memory records.
  Expected change site: `.github/workflows/orchestrate.yml` lines 233 and 359, `.github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml` line 322, `.github/workflows/orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml` line 282, `.github/workflows/validate.yml` lines 431-439, `.github/workflows/implement.yml` line 909
  Evidence of absence: `grep validation_discovery.v1.json .github/workflows/orchestrate.yml .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml .github/workflows/orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml .github/workflows/validate.yml .github/workflows/implement.yml` returns zero matches. All six schema fetch loops list only the legacy 9 schemas (`memory_record.v1.json`, `processed_command_entry.v1.json`, `run_ledger_entry.v1.json`, `task_lineage.v1.json`, `actions_runs_cache.v1.json`, `workflow_log_analysis_cache.v1.json`, `validation_history.v1.json`, `operator_bypass_audit.v1.json`, `revalidate_events.v1.json`). Without this schema bootstrapped to the `ai-memory` branch, `validate_validation_discovery_payload` in `scripts/ai_memory_lib.py` line 1018 calls `_validate_with_schema_file` which will fail on consumer repos that lack the schema file locally, causing discovery memory writes to be silently discarded.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
